Links I liked, week 41

Hi friends, a short one this week: six links, most of them about local-first software, and one about bread.

  • Local-first mail is having a moment — Why three new mail clients all keep your mailbox on your own disk, and what that buys you offline.

  • SQLite 3.51 release notes — Faster JSON functions and a new way to read the WAL from a second process.

  • Terminal workflows that stuck — A year of living in the terminal, and the three tools that survived it.

  • Why sync engines need tombstones — Deletes are the hard part, and the fix is from the eighties.

  • The quiet death of the three-pane layout — Every RSS reader since 2002 shipped the same window. What replaces it?

  • A sourdough schedule for people with jobs — Mix at night, shape in the morning, bake after work.

That's it. Reply and tell me what you're reading.
